title: Tomato and bread salad
method: Chop the tomatoes over a bowl to catch the juice, and salt them.
Tear in the bread and cucumber, and leave for ten minutes to soak up the juice.
Dress with oil and vinegar, and tear the basil over.

title: Slow-roasted tomatoes
ingredients: salt and a pinch of sugar
method: Lay the tomatoes cut side up on a tray, with the garlic and thyme.
Season, drizzle with oil, and roast at 120 °C for about three hours, until jammy.
Keep in a jar under oil in the fridge for a week, or freeze.

title: Green tomato chutney
method: Chop everything small and put it all in a heavy pan.
Simmer gently, stirring now and then, for about two hours, until thick and dark.
Spoon into warm, clean jars and seal. Leave a month before opening.

title: A sauce for the freezer
method: Soften the onion and garlic in oil.
Add the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 40 minutes, until thick.
Stir in the basil, blitz if you like, and freeze in bags flat.

title: Courgette ribbons with lemon and mint
method: Shave the courgettes into ribbons with a peeler.
Toss with lemon juice, oil, salt and torn mint.
Shave a little parmesan over and eat straight away.

title: Courgette fritters
method: Salt the grated courgette, leave ten minutes, then squeeze it dry.
Mix with the onion, dill, crumbled feta, egg and flour.
Fry spoonfuls in hot oil for three minutes a side.

title: Courgette and lemon cake
method: Whisk the eggs, sugar, oil and lemon zest.
Fold in the flour and courgette.
Bake in a lined loaf tin at 180 °C for about 45 minutes. Ice with lemon juice and icing sugar.

title: Runner beans in tomato
method: Soften the garlic in oil, then add the tomatoes.
Simmer for ten minutes, add the beans and a splash of water.
Cook gently for fifteen minutes, until the beans are soft and sweet.

title: Runner bean chutney
method: Slice the beans and boil until tender; drain.
Cook the onions in half the vinegar until soft.
Add the beans, the rest of the vinegar and the sugar, and simmer for fifteen minutes. Thicken with the spices mixed in a little vinegar with the cornflour, and jar.

title: French bean, potato and egg salad
method: Boil the potatoes; add the beans for the last four minutes.
Boil the eggs for seven minutes and halve them.
Toss everything warm with a mustard dressing and snipped chives.

title: Young broad beans with pecorino
ingredients: 300 g young broad beans in their pods
method: Pod the beans; the smallest are best raw.
Shave over the cheese, add a squeeze of lemon and good oil.
Eat in the sun.

title: Broad bean and mint smash on toast
method: Boil the beans for three minutes and slip off the grey skins.
Crush with mint, lemon, oil and salt.
Pile onto hot toast.

title: Peas braised with lettuce
method: Melt the butter and soften the onions.
Add the peas, lettuce and stock, and cover.
Cook for five minutes, until the peas are just tender.

title: Pea and mint soup
method: Soften the onion in butter.
Add the stock and peas, and simmer for five minutes only.
Blitz with the mint, and swirl in a little cream.

title: New potatoes with mint and butter
method: Scrub the potatoes; don't peel them.
Boil with the mint in salted water until tender.
Drain, and toss with butter and fresh chopped mint.

title: Rosemary roast potatoes
method: Par-boil the potatoes for eight minutes, drain and shake to rough them up.
Tip into hot fat with the rosemary and unpeeled garlic.
Roast at 200 °C for about an hour, turning once, until crisp.

title: Leek and potato soup
method: Melt the sliced leeks slowly in butter.
Add the diced potatoes and stock, and simmer for twenty minutes.
Blitz, or leave chunky, and scatter with chives.

title: Leeks with mustard dressing
method: Simmer the leeks until soft, then drain well.
Whisk the mustard, vinegar and oil.
Pour over the warm leeks, and finish with chopped egg and parsley.

title: Carrot and ginger soup
method: Soften the onion and ginger.
Add the sliced carrots and stock, and simmer until soft.
Blitz until smooth, and scatter with coriander.

title: Honey-roast carrots with thyme
method: Halve the carrots lengthways.
Toss with oil, honey, thyme and salt.
Roast at 200 °C for half an hour, until sticky at the edges.

title: Crunchy carrot slaw
method: Grate the carrots and shred the cabbage finely.
Stir the yoghurt, mayonnaise and lemon together.
Toss everything with the parsley.

title: Roast parsnips with honey
method: Cut the parsnips into long wedges.
Roast in hot oil at 200 °C for half an hour.
Drizzle with honey for the last ten minutes.

title: Spiced parsnip soup
method: Soften the onion with the curry powder.
Add the parsnips and stock, and simmer until soft.
Blitz with a little cream.

title: Roast beetroot with goat's cheese
method: Wrap the beetroot in foil and roast at 200 °C for 45 minutes.
Peel while warm and cut into wedges.
Toss with the rocket, crumble over the cheese and walnuts, and dress.

title: Quick pickled beetroot
method: Boil the beetroot until tender, peel and slice.
Heat the vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved.
Pack the beetroot in a jar, pour over the hot vinegar and seal. Keeps in the fridge for a month.

title: Radishes with butter and salt
method: Wash the radishes, leaving a little leaf as a handle.
Dip in soft butter, then in salt.
Eat with bread. That's it.

title: A garden leaf salad
ingredients: two big handfuls of mixed leaves
method: Pick the leaves in the cool of the morning and wash gently.
Whisk the mustard, vinegar and oil.
Dress at the last minute, with sliced radish and snipped chives.

title: Griddled little gems
method: Halve the lettuces and brush with oil.
Griddle cut side down for two minutes, until charred.
Squeeze over lemon and scatter with chives and parmesan.

title: Spinach with garlic and lemon
method: Warm the sliced garlic in oil until just golden.
Add the spinach and stir until it wilts.
Season and squeeze over lemon.

title: Chard gratin
method: Slice the stems and cook for five minutes; add the leaves for the last two.
Make a white sauce with the butter, flour and milk, and add the garlic.
Mix with the chard, top with cheese and bake at 200 °C for twenty minutes.

title: Kale crisps
method: Strip the leaves from the stalks and tear into pieces.
Massage with oil, salt and chilli.
Bake in one layer at 150 °C for fifteen minutes, until crisp.

title: Pasta with kale, garlic and chilli
method: Boil the kale with the pasta for the last five minutes.
Warm the garlic and chilli in plenty of oil.
Drain, toss everything together with a splash of pasta water and parmesan.

title: Bean and cavolo nero soup
method: Soften the chopped carrot, celery and onion in oil.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock, and simmer for twenty minutes.
Add the shredded cavolo nero and torn bread, and cook for fifteen minutes more, until thick.

title: Red cabbage with apple
method: Shred the cabbage and slice the apple and onion.
Layer in a pan with the vinegar, sugar and spice.
Cover and cook very gently for an hour and a half, stirring now and then.

title: Sauerkraut
method: Shred the cabbage finely and rub it with the salt until it gives up its juice.
Pack tightly into a clean jar with the caraway, pressing it under the juice.
Leave at room temperature for one to three weeks, tasting as it sours, then keep in the fridge.

title: Sprouting broccoli with anchovy butter
method: Mash the anchovies and garlic into the soft butter.
Steam the broccoli for four minutes.
Toss with the butter until it melts, and add a squeeze of lemon.

title: Charred broccoli with chilli
method: Cut the broccoli into long florets and toss in oil.
Roast at 220 °C for fifteen minutes, until the edges char.
Toss with sliced chilli, garlic and lemon.

title: Whole roast cauliflower
method: Trim the cauliflower, keeping the small leaves, and boil whole for five minutes.
Rub with oil and spices, and roast at 200 °C for about an hour.
Serve with yoghurt and parsley.

title: Cauliflower cheese
method: Boil the florets for five minutes and drain well.
Make a white sauce, and stir in most of the cheese and the mustard.
Pour over the cauliflower, top with the rest of the cheese and bake at 200 °C for twenty minutes.

title: Sprouts with bacon and chestnuts
method: Halve the sprouts and boil for three minutes; drain.
Fry the bacon until crisp, then add the sprouts and chestnuts.
Fry hard for five minutes until browned, with a knob of butter.

title: Roast squash and sage soup
method: Roast the squash in chunks at 200 °C for 40 minutes.
Soften the onion, add the squash and stock, and blitz.
Fry the sage leaves crisp in oil and float them on top.

title: Squash wedges with chilli and feta
method: Cut the squash into wedges, skin on.
Roast with oil and chilli at 200 °C for 35 minutes.
Crumble over the feta and drizzle with honey.

title: Pumpkin soup
method: Soften the onion and garlic.
Add the cubed pumpkin and stock, and simmer until soft.
Blitz, and season with nutmeg.

title: Stuffed marrow
method: Halve the marrow lengthways and scoop out the seeds.
Fry the onion with the mince or lentils and chopped tomatoes.
Fill the marrow, top with cheese, cover and bake at 180 °C for 45 minutes.

title: Tzatziki
method: Grate the cucumber, salt it and squeeze out the water.
Stir into the yoghurt with the crushed garlic and mint.
Finish with a little oil.

title: Quick dill pickles
method: Slice the cucumbers and pack into a jar with the dill and garlic.
Heat the vinegar, water, salt and sugar until dissolved.
Pour over, cool and keep in the fridge. Ready the next day.

title: Corn on the cob with chilli butter
method: Boil the cobs for four minutes.
Mash the butter with the chopped chilli and lime zest.
Roll the hot cobs in the butter.

title: Sweetcorn fritters
method: Cut the kernels from the cobs.
Mix with the onions, coriander, egg and flour.
Fry spoonfuls in hot oil until golden.

title: Chilli jam
method: Blitz the chillies, peppers and ginger finely.
Boil with the sugar and vinegar for about 40 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Jar while hot. Good with cheese.

title: Roast peppers in oil
method: Roast the whole peppers at 220 °C until blackened, then cover to steam.
Peel and tear into strips.
Layer with sliced garlic and basil, cover with oil and keep in the fridge for a week.

title: Smoky aubergine dip
method: Char the aubergines whole over a flame or under the grill until collapsed.
Scoop out the flesh and mash with garlic, tahini and lemon.
Top with parsley and oil.

title: Asparagus with a soft egg
method: Boil the eggs for six minutes.
Steam or griddle the asparagus for three or four minutes.
Dip the spears into the yolks, with butter and salt.

title: Slow onion and thyme tart
method: Cook the sliced onions very slowly in butter for 40 minutes, until sweet and golden.
Spread over the pastry, leaving a border, and scatter with thyme and cheese.
Bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes.

title: Pickled shallots
method: Peel the shallots (soak them in hot water first) and salt overnight.
Rinse and pack into jars.
Boil the vinegar, sugar and spice, pour over and seal. Ready in a month.

title: Roast garlic
method: Slice the tops off the bulbs.
Drizzle with oil, add thyme, and wrap in foil.
Roast at 180 °C for 45 minutes, then squeeze the soft cloves onto bread.

title: Spring onion pancakes
method: Mix the flour and hot water into a dough, and rest it for twenty minutes.
Roll thin, brush with sesame oil, scatter with onions and salt, roll up and coil.
Flatten and fry until crisp on both sides.

title: Swede and carrot mash
method: Cube the swede and carrots and boil until soft.
Drain well and mash roughly with butter.
Season hard with pepper.

title: Celeriac remoulade
method: Peel the celeriac and cut into fine matchsticks.
Toss straight away with lemon juice.
Stir in the mayonnaise, mustard and parsley.

title: Fennel and orange salad
method: Shave the fennel as thin as you can.
Cut the orange into slices over the bowl to catch the juice.
Toss with olives and oil, and scatter the fronds over.

title: Pak choi with garlic and soy
method: Halve the pak choi lengthways.
Fry the garlic, then add the pak choi and a splash of water; cover for two minutes.
Dress with soy and sesame oil.

title: Kohlrabi and apple slaw
method: Peel the kohlrabi and cut it and the apple into matchsticks.
Toss with lemon juice straight away.
Stir in the yoghurt and torn mint.

title: Glazed baby turnips
method: Halve the turnips, keeping a little stalk.
Simmer in a shallow pan with butter, sugar and water to come halfway up.
Boil off the water until they're glossy and golden.

title: Jerusalem artichoke soup
method: Scrub and slice the artichokes; drop into water with lemon.
Soften the onion, add the artichokes and stock, and simmer until soft.
Blitz with a little cream: silky and nutty.

title: Smoky sweet potato wedges
method: Cut into wedges, skin on.
Toss with oil, paprika and salt.
Roast at 200 °C for half an hour.

title: Green tomatillo salsa
method: Husk the tomatillos and grill until blistered.
Blitz with the chilli, onion, coriander and lime.
Salt to taste. Freezes well.

title: Edamame with sea salt
method: Boil the pods in salted water for four minutes.
Drain and toss with salt and chilli.
Squeeze the beans out with your teeth.

title: Mangetout and spring onion stir-fry
method: Get a pan very hot with a little oil.
Stir-fry the ginger for a few seconds, then the mangetout and onions for two minutes.
Add a splash of soy and serve straight away.

title: Watercress soup
method: Soften the onion, add the diced potato and stock, and simmer until soft.
Add the watercress for just two minutes.
Blitz until bright green.

title: Braised chicory with orange
method: Halve the chicory lengthways and brown in butter.
Add the orange juice and sugar, and cover.
Cook gently for twenty minutes, until soft and caramelised.

title: Fresh borlotti beans with sage
method: Pod the beans.
Simmer with the sage and garlic in water to cover for 30 minutes, until creamy.
Drain, and dress with plenty of good oil and salt.

title: Quick kimchi
method: Chop the cabbage, rub with salt and leave two hours; rinse and squeeze.
Mix the garlic, ginger, chilli and fish sauce into a paste.
Toss everything together, pack into a jar and leave a day or two before the fridge.

title: Basil pesto
method: Blitz the basil, garlic and nuts.
Add the cheese and oil, and blitz again briefly.
Use straight away, or freeze in ice-cube trays.

title: Salsa verde
ingredients: a few mint and basil leaves
method: Chop the herbs, garlic, capers and anchovies together finely.
Stir in the mustard, a splash of vinegar and oil to loosen.
Spoon over fish, lamb or new potatoes.

title: Herb tabbouleh
method: Soak the bulgur in a little boiling water for ten minutes.
Chop the herbs, tomatoes and onions finely.
Mix with the bulgur, plenty of lemon, oil and salt. It should be mostly green.

title: Mint sauce
method: Chop the mint finely with the sugar.
Add the boiling water, then the vinegar.
Leave for half an hour before serving with lamb.

title: Fresh mint tea
method: Bruise the leaves in a pot.
Pour over just-boiled water and leave for five minutes.
Sweeten with honey if you like.

title: Garden herb butter
method: Chop the herbs and garlic finely.
Beat into the butter with the lemon zest and salt.
Roll in baking paper and freeze in slices for steak, fish or bread.

title: Pasta with sage and brown butter
method: Cook the pasta.
Heat the butter with the sage until it smells nutty and the leaves crisp.
Toss with the pasta, a splash of its water and parmesan.

title: New potatoes with dill and soured cream
method: Boil the potatoes until tender.
Stir the chopped dill and lemon into the soured cream.
Spoon over the warm potatoes.

title: Green coriander chutney
method: Blitz everything with a splash of water.
Season with salt and more lime.
Good with curries, eggs and grilled things.

title: Sorrel sauce for fish
method: Melt the shredded sorrel in the butter: it turns khaki, which is fine.
Stir in the cream and bubble for a minute.
Spoon over fish, or eggs.

title: Horseradish cream
method: Peel and grate the root finely (open a window).
Stir into the crème fraîche with the vinegar and sugar.
Serve with roast beef or smoked fish.

title: Strawberries with black pepper and cream
method: Hull and halve the strawberries.
Sprinkle with sugar and a little pepper, and leave ten minutes.
Serve with cream.

title: Strawberry jam
method: Hull the berries and crush a few in a big pan with the sugar and lemon juice.
Heat gently until the sugar dissolves, then boil hard for about eight minutes, until it wrinkles on a cold plate.
Leave fifteen minutes, then jar.

title: Eton mess
method: Crush half the fruit with a fork.
Whip the cream softly and crumble in the meringue.
Fold in the fruit, crushed and whole, and serve straight away.

title: Raspberries with honey and yoghurt
method: Crush half the raspberries into the yoghurt.
Top with the rest, a drizzle of honey and the oats.

title: Summer pudding
ingredients: 800 g mixed summer berries and currants
method: Simmer the fruit with the sugar for three minutes, until the juice runs.
Line a bowl with bread, fill with fruit and juice, and cover with more bread.
Weigh down overnight in the fridge, then turn out.

title: Blackcurrant cordial
method: Simmer the currants in the water for ten minutes, crushing them.
Strain through a cloth, add the sugar and lemon juice, and heat until dissolved.
Bottle and keep in the fridge. Dilute to taste.

title: Gooseberry fool
method: Cook the gooseberries with the sugar until they burst, then cool.
Whip the cream softly.
Ripple the fruit through the cream.

title: Blueberry muffins
method: Whisk the wet ingredients, then stir into the flour and sugar until just mixed.
Fold in the blueberries.
Bake in muffin cases at 200 °C for twenty minutes.

title: Rhubarb and ginger crumble
method: Chop the rhubarb and toss with the sugar and grated ginger in a dish.
Rub the butter into the flour, then stir in the oats and brown sugar.
Scatter over and bake at 190 °C for 35 minutes.

title: Roast rhubarb with orange
method: Cut the rhubarb into short lengths and lay in a dish.
Add the orange zest and juice, and the sugar.
Roast at 180 °C for fifteen minutes, until just tender. Good with yoghurt.

title: Blackberry and apple crumble
method: Peel and slice the apples, and toss with the berries and sugar in a dish.
Rub the butter into the flour and stir in the brown sugar.
Scatter over and bake at 190 °C for 35 minutes.

title: Baked apples
method: Core the apples and score a line round their middles.
Fill with sultanas, sugar and cinnamon, and top with butter.
Bake at 180 °C for 40 minutes, until fluffy.

title: Apple chutney
method: Peel and chop the apples and onions.
Simmer everything gently for about an hour and a half, until thick.
Jar while hot, and keep a month before opening.

title: Pears with blue cheese and walnuts
method: Slice the pears.
Lay on the rocket with the crumbled cheese and walnuts.
Drizzle with honey and a little oil.

title: Pears poached in red wine
method: Peel the pears, leaving the stalks.
Simmer gently in the wine with the sugar and spices for 30 minutes, turning them.
Boil the liquid down to a syrup and pour over.

title: Roast plums with honey
method: Halve and stone the plums and lay in a dish.
Drizzle with honey and juice, and add the cinnamon.
Roast at 200 °C for twenty minutes. With yoghurt or ice cream.

title: Plum jam
method: Simmer the halved fruit in the water until soft (fish out damson stones as they rise).
Add the sugar, stir until dissolved, then boil hard until it wrinkles on a cold plate.
Jar while hot.

title: Damson gin
method: Prick each damson with a fork.
Put in a big jar with the sugar and gin.
Shake every few days for a month, then leave somewhere dark until Christmas. Strain and bottle.

title: Cherry clafoutis
method: Butter a dish and scatter in the cherries (stones in, if you like: they add flavour).
Whisk the eggs, sugar, flour and milk into a batter and pour over.
Bake at 180 °C for 35 minutes, until puffed and golden.

title: Figs with ham and honey
method: Tear the figs open.
Lay with the ham and rocket.
Drizzle with honey and a little oil.

title: Quince cheese
ingredients: sugar (the same weight as the purée)
method: Simmer the chopped quinces in water until very soft, then sieve to a purée.
Weigh it, add the same weight of sugar and the lemon juice, and cook very gently, stirring, until thick and deep orange (about two hours).
Set in a lined tin. Slice and eat with cheese.

title: Grape and rosemary focaccia
method: Mix the flour, yeast, water and salt, and leave to rise for an hour.
Stretch into an oiled tin, press in grapes and rosemary, and rise for half an hour.
Drizzle with oil and salt and bake at 220 °C for twenty minutes.

title: Baked apricots with almonds
method: Halve and stone the apricots and lay in a dish.
Drizzle with honey, dot with butter and scatter with almonds.
Bake at 190 °C for twenty minutes.

title: Grilled peaches with mascarpone
method: Halve and stone the peaches.
Griddle cut side down for three minutes, until marked.
Serve with mascarpone, honey and mint.

title: Redcurrant jelly
ingredients: sugar (450 g for every 600 ml of juice)
method: Simmer the currants in the water until soft, then strain through a cloth overnight. Don't squeeze it.
Measure the juice, add the sugar, and boil hard until it sets on a cold plate.
Jar while hot. Good with lamb.

title: Bramble jelly
ingredients: sugar (450 g for every 600 ml of juice)
method: Simmer the berries and chopped apples in a little water until soft, then strain overnight.
Add the sugar and lemon juice to the juice, and boil hard until it sets.
Jar while hot.

title: A garden fruit smoothie
ingredients: two handfuls of berries, fresh or frozen
method: Blitz everything until smooth.
Sweeten with honey if it needs it.

title: Chamomile tea
ingredients: 2 tbsp dried chamomile flowers (or a small handful fresh)
method: Pour just-boiled water over the flowers.
Cover and leave for five minutes, then strain.
A spoon of honey, and bed.

title: Lemon verbena cream
ingredients: a handful of lemon verbena leaves
method: Warm the cream with the leaves and sugar, then leave to cool and infuse.
Strain, chill, and whip softly.
Serve with strawberries.

title: Chicken with tarragon and cream
method: Brown the chicken, then soften the chopped shallots in the same pan.
Add the wine and let it bubble, then the cream.
Simmer until the chicken is cooked through, and stir in the chopped tarragon.

title: Scrambled eggs with chives
method: Whisk the eggs with a little salt.
Cook slowly in the butter, stirring, until just set.
Snip over plenty of chives, and pile on toast.

title: Garden minestrone
method: Soften the chopped onion and carrots.
Add the tomatoes and stock, and simmer for fifteen minutes.
Add the pasta, courgette and beans for the last ten minutes, and finish with basil.

title: Ratatouille
method: Fry each vegetable separately in oil until golden, and set aside.
Soften the onion and garlic, add the tomatoes, and cook down for ten minutes.
Return everything with the thyme and simmer gently for 40 minutes. Better the next day.

title: A late-summer tray bake
method: Halve the potatoes and roast with oil at 200 °C for twenty minutes.
Add the courgettes, onions, rosemary and sausages, and roast for twenty minutes more.
Add the tomatoes for the last ten minutes.

title: Winter roots with thyme
method: Cut everything into chunks of a similar size.
Toss with oil, thyme and salt.
Roast at 200 °C for 40 minutes, turning once.

title: Bubble and squeak
method: Mash the potato with the chopped greens.
Press into a hot buttered pan and leave to crisp for ten minutes before turning.
Serve with a fried egg.

title: Spring greens soup
method: Soften the onion, add the diced potato and stock, and simmer until soft.
Add the greens for three minutes only.
Blitz until bright green, and swirl in the cream.

title: Lettuce soup
method: Soften the onions in butter.
Add the stock and peas, and simmer for five minutes.
Add the shredded lettuce for two minutes, then blitz.

title: Rocket pesto
method: Blitz the rocket, garlic and walnuts.
Add the cheese, oil and a squeeze of lemon, and blitz briefly.
Peppery with pasta or on a sandwich.

title: Beetroot chocolate cake
method: Melt the chocolate and butter; blitz the beetroot smooth.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then stir in the chocolate and beetroot.
Fold in the flour and cocoa, and bake at 180 °C for 45 minutes.
